3. Plaintiffs' case in short is that .06 1/2and half decimals of land out of .11 decimals of plot no. 288,..13 decimal of land out 1.10 acres of plot no.290 totaling .19-2 decimals of land of C.S. Khatian No.76 of Mouza Sonatia, P.S. Kotalipara, is the suit land. During R.S. record the above lands of the Sonatia Mouza have been recorded in R.S. Plot Nos.330 and 332 respectively of R.S. Khatian No. 46. During S.A. operation the above lands have been recorded in S.A. Khatian no. 41 of mouza Sonatia. One Asalat' Shaikh was the owner of the said land at the time of C.S. operation and the above lands were correctly recorded in the name of Asalat Shaikh. Asalat Saikh had 4.77 acre of land in the said C.S. Khatian including the suit land. Asalat Shaikh had two wives. Asalat Shaik ad three sons namely Sahar Ali, Taher Ali and Wahed Ali by first wife and three sons namely Yasinuddin Saikh, Shujaruddin Shaikh, Budai Shaikh and one daughter Baru Bibi by second wife. After the death of Asalat Sheik, his above mentioned sons and daughter inherited his whole properties. While they were in peaceful possession of the suit land, Yasinuddin Shaikh, Shujaruddin Shaikh, Budhai Shaikh and Baru Bibi sons and daughter respectively of Asalat Shaikh by his second wife sold the suit land totaling .19Y2 decimals of land to the predecessors of the plaintiffs Jalaluddin Shaikh and Shafizuddin Shaikh both sons of late Jaban ullah Shaikh vide kabala no.4897 dated 18.8.1943 and handed over possession. The suitland has been recorded in the names of the said Jalaludddin Sheikh and Shafizuddin Shaikh in R.S. Khatian No. 46 and S.A. Khatian No.41 along wit other co-sharers; But due to mistake Jalaluddin Shaikh and Shafizuddin Shaikh's possession was not noted in the remarks column of the said .khatians. The said entries in the remarks column of the R.S. Khatian and S.A. Khatian are erroneous. 

 4. Shafizuddin Shaikh died leaving three sons plaintiff nos.1-3 and two daughters plaintiff no.4 and 5. On the other hand Jalaluddin Shaikh died leaving plaintiff nos.6 and 7 as his heirs. The plaintiffs have been possessing the homestead land by constructing house and living thereon along with their family members and the rest land is being possessed by cultivation. The defendants threatened, to dispossess 'the plaintiff on 15.5.95 disclosing the wrong entries in the remarks column of R.S. and S.A Khatians. Hence the plaintiffs have filed the suit. 

 5. The defendant no. I and 14 (0.P.No.1 and 2) contested the suit by filing joint written statement contending inter alia that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and the suit is barred by limitation and bad for defect of parties. The defence case is that Asalat Shaikh the C.S. Tenant of C.S. Khatian No.76 while in possession of his, share of the land of the said katian died leaving three sons, Shahar Ali, Taher Ali and Wahed Ali by first wife and 3 sons Yasinuddin Shaikh, Budhai Saikh and Sujaruddin Shaikh and 'one daughter Baru Bibi by second wife who inherited Asalat Sheikh's properties. Asalat Sheik's share of the land has "been recorded in R.S. khatian no.46 in five, groups correctly in the names of his heirs. Shafizuddin and Jalaluddin by registered exchange deed no.577 dated 13.2.48 gave .05 acre out of plot no. 332 of R.S. Khatian No.46 to defendant no.1 and his brother Abdul Karim son of Shahar Ali and Hafiz Shaikh and Shafizuddin and Jalaluddin got 22 decimal of plot no. 328 of  R.S. Khatian No.46. Plaintiffs' predecessors Jalaluddin and Shafizuddin acquired title and possession in .061/2 decimals of land of plot no.322 and 330 from the sons and daughter of the second wife of Asalat Shaikh. While, 41alaluddin and Shafijuddin were in possession of the said land partition deed no.2585 dated 3.10.1951 was executed amongst the co-sharers. Jalaluddin and Shafizuddin were 5th party in tat partition deed. Shafizuddin 241/2 acre of land with .2 and half' acre of land of R.S. plot no.332 vide patta deed dated 5.3.1955 in favour of some of the defendant's predecessors and the said patta purchased land has been recorded in S.A. Khatian in the names of the defendants predecessors. Yasin Shaik and others have never executed the kabala-dated 18.g.43 and the said kabala dated .18.8.43 is a forged one. The plaintiffs have no right, title and possession in the suit land. So, the suit land is liable to be dismissed. 

 9. At the time of hearing both the learned Counsels for the parties submit that there is no dispute regarding exchange deed dated 13.2.1948 for .05 decimal of land of R. S. Plot no. 332 of Khatian No.46. The learned Advocate for the petitioner mainly argued that the bone of contention between the parties is the registered patta alleged to have been executed between Ibraim Sheikh and Shafizuddin Sheikh on 6.3.1956 corresponding to 22nd Falgun, 1362 B.S. The learned Advocate for the petitioners argued that after the whole sale acquisition of rent receiving interest by notification no.18636 dated 13.12.1955 under section 17 (3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act a tenant had no right to give under tenancy as per provision of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The learned Advocate for the opposite parties tried to argue that the registered patta Ext. Kha (3) was executed on 3.6.1955 and not in 1956 as argued by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has drawn my attention to the back page of the stamp paper of patta. It appears that the stamp paper was purchased on 22.2.1956 on which the patta was written. So it goes without saying that the patta cannot be written before purchase of the stamp paper. Moreover, learned Advocate for the petitioner has referred to the judgment of the appellate court below and submits that in the judgment the Court of appellate below it was stated. that the defendants-opposite parties by firisti filed calendar of the year 1956 and on perusal of the calendar it appears that 22"IFalgu, 1362 corresponding to 6,3.1956 B.S. It is not disputed that the Bengali date 22nd Falgun 1362 was correctly written as the date of execution of patta. So, it is clear that the patta was written and executed on 22nd Falgun 1362 B.S corresponding to 6.3.1956. Therefore, from the evidence of defendant-opposite parties it was amply proved that the patta in question was executed oil 22'd Falgun 1362. B.S. corresponding to 6.3.1956 but as per provision of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act after the whole sale acquisition of rent receiving interest by notification no. 18636 dated 13.12.1955 no under tenancy could be created. In this view of this matter the patta in question is not a valid document in the eye law and it conveyed no title. Being faced to the situation the learned advocate for the defendant-opposite parties finds it difficult to argue that the patta is a genuine document as it was executed in 1956: Hence his, client is not entitled to get the land conveyed by this patta.
